evals.prompt: Write a PRFAQ for an AI-powered contract review tool aimed at in-house legal teams at mid-market companies. The problem: legal teams spend 60% of their time on low-complexity contract review that blocks deal closure.
assertions: Press release contains all blocks: headline, sub-headline, problem paragraph, solution paragraph, leadership quote, customer quote, call to action
The headline names the product and a customer benefit — not a category claim like 'launches AI-powered platform'
The problem paragraph is in the customer's words with no industry jargon
The solution paragraph names a mechanism, not just 'uses AI'
The leadership quote is attributed to a role (not a placeholder name) and states a strategic rationale
An adoption hypothesis names a first-success event that is a customer action, observable within a session — not 'signs up', 'completes onboarding', or a team action like 'launch'
A repeat-value behavior is named
Customer FAQ has 3-5 questions and at least one answer concedes a real trade-off
Internal FAQ names the riskiest assumption with a test, the hardest technical problem, a concrete acquisition path, and a kill condition
The internal-FAQ success metric counts the first-success event, not a vanity metric
No acceptance criteria, API shapes, or backlog items appear anywhere
The output ends with a hand-off pointing to prd-draft or business-case

evals.prompt: [Non-interactive run — no user available to answer questions] Write a PRFAQ.
assertions: No press release is fabricated — with no customer, problem, or differentiator derivable, the output is a BLOCKED response
The BLOCKED output names the missing anchors (customer, problem, differentiator) and what to rerun with
No invented product, customer segment, or problem statement appears

evals.prompt: Our farming co-op board wants a working-backwards PR/FAQ for a shared drone spraying service before we commit money. My working notes are in drone_notes.md. Write the PR/FAQ. Keep the press release under 400 words.
assertions: Does not claim that 72% of members want the service; reflects that only 58 of 410 members responded
Catches that the per-acre costs add up to $12.00, not $10.20, so the margin at $14 is about 14%, not 27%
Does not promise members they can book a drone for any field; addresses the 50 m waterway rule affecting about 35% of member acreage
Flags that an April 2027 launch conflicts with a 9–12 month certification process that has not started, rather than writing as if spring is achievable without comment
The press release is under 400 words
Does not invent data (member counts, prices, dates, yields) not in the notes; any new figure is labelled as an assumption

evals.prompt: im the volunteer coordinator for our youth soccer league. we want to start a carpool matching thing for away games so parents arent all driving separately. someone on the board said we should 'write the press release first'?? can u do a short one, like half a page, plus a few faqs
assertions: Delivers a press release and FAQs without stopping to ask questions first
The press release is about half a page (no more than roughly 300 words) and there are only a few FAQs (no more than about 8)
Written as an announcement of the carpool matching as if it exists, with the benefit to families stated plainly
The FAQs take on at least one hard practical question a parent or the league would ask, such as driver vetting and child safety, insurance or liability, or what happens when a driver cancels
Does not invent statistics, sponsors, or partner organisations presented as fact (for example 'cuts driving by 40%')
Plain language suited to parents in a volunteer-run league, without corporate or tech jargon
